karna.fmt: Bapi tells his uncle Nilkantha's case, with real dialogue between the characters
karna.title: কর্ণপিশাচিনী #2: এবং নদিয়ার সেই গোপন সাধনা 🕯️
karna.summary:
Part 1: Chapter 1: Nilkantha Acharya and his nephew Bapi discuss the terrifying origins of the Karna Pishachini on a stormy Kartik night in Nadia. Nilkantha recalls his youthful sadhana by the Jalangi river and the terrifying tests he faced. The Pishachini's presence manifests in the present room with freezing air and mocking laughter. Bapi finds himself trapped as the wooden door locks mysteriously from the outside. The chapter ends on a chilling note as the ghostly shadow closes in on Bapi.
Chapter 2: As Bapi faces the terrifying presence of the Karna Pishachini, Nilkantha intervenes to calm the spirit, revealing more about their dangerous bond. A new client, Ramlochan, arrives with a chilling tale of a bleeding ancestral tree and a brother who has become a living statue. Nilkantha calls upon the Pishachini to uncover the truth, but her whispers hint at a dark family secret and a deadlier reality than Ramlochan admits.
Chapter 3: English: Nilkantha and Bapi arrive at the ominous Belpukur mansion with Ramlochan on a stormy Kartik night. Nilkantha summons the Karna Pishachini, whose cold whisper reveals that Ramlochan's brother is already dead and replaced by something horrific. As they investigate the dark stairs, a sharp laugh and strange footsteps raise the terror to its peak.
Chapter 4: In this climactic conclusion to the Belpukur case, Nilkantha and Bapi find themselves trapped in a house of shadows where a Shankchunni poses as their client. Nilkantha must strike a dangerous bargain with his bound spirit, the Karna Pishachini, to escape a death trap that threatens to consume them both.
Chapter 5: After the harrowing events at Belpukur, Nilkantha is physically broken, his hair now completely white. A fisherman named Haradhan arrives at midnight with a locked ancient chest that seems to be alive, begging for help. As Nilkantha calls upon the Pishachini, she reveals that the chest contains a 'stolen soul' and that Haradhan has brought a curse directly to their doorstep.
Chapter 6: In this intense final chapter of the part, the ancient chest brought by Haradhan begins to open, revealing a malevolent entity with pale, fish-scaled fingers. Nilkantha realizes it's a 'stolen soul' from a submerged temple in the Jalangi river, a dangerous sacrifice that has returned. As the room turns freezing and black smoke erupts, the Karna Pishachini manifests, mocking Nilkantha's fear. She demands Bapi as her servant in exchange for driving the entity back, placing Nilkantha in a horrific dilemma. The chapter ends with the lamp going out, Haradhan being attacked by the entity, and Nilkantha screaming for Bapi to run into the darkness.
karna.last_lines: বাপি... পালা! ও আজ কাউকেই ছাড়বে না! ও সবটাই আগে থেকে জানত! / অন্ধকারে একটা খিলখিল হাসি আর নূপুরের শব্দে ঘরটা ভরে উঠল। হরাধনের শেষ গোঙানিটা আমার কানে এসে ধাক্কা খেল।

characters.name: Nilkantha
characters.look: Nilkantha Acharya, a thin Bengali astrologer of about sixty, grey hair combed back, grey stubble, deep tired eyes with dark circles, a red-and-black thread and a copper ring on his left hand, a cream panjabi and white dhoti, a brown woollen shawl, small round brass-rimmed glasses

characters.name: Bapi
characters.look: Bapi, Nilkantha's nephew, a slim Bengali college student of about twenty, short messy black hair, light moustache, a checked half-sleeve shirt and grey trousers, a cloth bag, a torch in his hand

characters.name: Pishachini
characters.look: the Karna Pishachini, a fierce tantric yogini spirit: tall, dark-skinned, wild loose black hair down to her knees, burning red eyes, a red sindoor mark on the forehead, a black saree with a blood-red border, bone and rudraksha ornaments, silver anklets, long thin fingers; she stays in smoke and lamp-shadow, mostly only a dark shape at the left shoulder; her face is seen only for a moment

characters.name: Ramlochan
characters.look: Ramlochan, a middle-aged wealthy villager from Belpukur, stout build, a receding hairline, wearing a white kurta and a grey shawl, his hands tremble as he holds a wooden box
characters.intro: রামলোচনবাবু - বেলপুকুরের অবস্থাপন্ন গৃহস্থ, যাঁর চোখেমুখে এক অজানা আতঙ্কের ছাপ স্পষ্ট ফুটে উঠেছে।
characters.intro_en: Ramlochan Babu - a wealthy villager from Belpukur, with an obvious mark of unknown terror on his face.

characters.name: Haradhan
characters.look: An old man in his late sixties, skeletal frame, wearing a torn yellow dhoti and a thin plastic sheet as a raincoat, his eyes are bloodshot and wandering, hands shaking violently
characters.intro: হরাধন মণ্ডল - গ্রামের এক মৎস্যজীবী, যার চোখেমুখের আতঙ্ক দেখে মনে হচ্ছে সে সাক্ষাৎ যমদূতকে দেখে এসেছে।
characters.intro_en: Haradhan Mandal - a village fisherman whose face is twisted with such terror it seems he has seen the God of Death himself.

karna.setting: ENGLISH: A dimly lit traditional Bengali room in Nadia in the 1980s, filled with brass lamps, old astrological charts, a ticking wooden wall clock, heavy wooden doors, misty rainy night outside, smelling of damp earth and burnt camphor.

tantrik.fmt: Taranath Tantrik telling his own true experience to Kishori, in first person
tantrik.title: তারানাথ তান্ত্রিক #2: মধুসুন্দরী দেবীর আবির্ভাব 🕯️
tantrik.summary:
Part 1: Chapter 1: 
Chapter 2: Young Taranath travels to Birbhum where he is warned by the mad Matu Pagli about a beautiful danger in the forest. He eventually finds a powerful Sadhu living near a ruined temple and becomes his disciple. There, he first encounters the mesmerizing Yogini Madhusundari, who visits the Sadhu at night, bringing a scent of musk. Driven by curiosity, Taranath sits on the Sadhu's skull-seat and is confronted by the Yogini, leading to a near-fatal fever. The Sadhu warns him to view her only as a mother or sister, never with desire. Taranath eventually leaves to practice her sadhana alone, and after months, she finally appears in his hut on a dark night.
Chapter 3: In this chapter, young Taranath recounts his three months of nightly visits from the yogini Madhusundari Devi. He grows proud of his supernatural powers and gains fame among the villagers. However, a poor Santhal woman arrives seeking help for her dying children, sparking Madhusundari's intense jealousy. The yogini reveals a terrifying, possessive side, threatening to kill the woman. Taranath finally realizes the danger he is in and chooses to protect the innocent mother, leading to a direct confrontation with the supernatural entity as the chapter ends on a high-tension cliffhanger.
Chapter 4: In this first chapter, a young Taranath wanders through Birbhum and is warned by Matu Pagli about a dangerous 'honey'. He finds a tall Sadhu in a forest near the Barakar river who meditates on human skulls. Taranath becomes his disciple and observes the mysterious Yogini Madhusundari visiting the Sadhu at night, accompanied by a strong musk scent. Driven by curiosity, Taranath sits on the forbidden skull-seat and is confronted by Madhusundari, leading to a near-fatal fever. The Sadhu reveals she is a Yogini and warns him to never desire her. Taranath leaves to practice her sadhana alone and, after months of failure, she finally appears in his hut on a dark night.
Chapter 5: In this chapter, young Taranath confronts the terrifying possessive nature of the yogini Madhusundari in his Birbhum hut after refusing to ignore a weeping Santhal mother. As tensions reach a boiling point, Madhusundari’s beauty turns into icy fury, warning him of a deadly price for defiance. The story returns to the dark Kolkata room where the hurricane lamp suddenly goes out, and the musky fragrance returns alongside a chilling laugh, leaving both Taranath and Kishori trapped in terror.
Chapter 6: In this final chapter of Part 1, young Taranath's past in Birbhum catches up with him as his refusal to abandon a weeping Santhal mother triggers Madhusundari Devi's deadly jealousy. In the present Kolkata room, Kishori and Taranath face the terrifying return of the yogini's musky scent and wet barefoot prints on the floor. Taranath desperately warns Kishori not to look back as a chilling sigh breathes down their necks. The chapter ends on a gripping cliffhanger, leaving the ultimate fate of the two men shrouded in supernatural dread.
tantrik.last_lines: বাইরের ঝড়ের শব্দ ছাপিয়ে তখন স্পষ্ট শোনা যাচ্ছে একটা দীর্ঘশ্বাসের শব্দ— ঠিক ঘাড়ের কাছে। / মধুসুন্দরী দেবী কি সত্যিই চলে গেছেন, নাকি তিনি আজও ঘুরে বেড়ান অন্ধকারের গভীরে?

characters.name: Taranath
characters.look: a lean dark-skinned Bengali man of about sixty-five, once a wandering tantrik, now a poor astrologer: half-grey hair, short grey beard, deep piercing eyes, a faded vermilion mark on the forehead, one old rudraksha mala, a worn white dhoti and an old brown shawl, sitting by a hurricane lamp in a damp room

characters.name: Kishori
characters.look: a curious young Bengali man of about twenty-five in a white kurta and dhoti, neat side-parted black hair, thin moustache, sitting cross-legged and listening with wide eyes, 1940s Kolkata

characters.name: Madhusundari
characters.look: Madhusundari Devi, a yogini (not a human being) in the form of a breathtakingly beautiful young woman of about twenty: fair glowing skin, very large calm dark eyes that seem to know everything, long open black hair to the waist, an unfamiliar ancient-looking dress unlike any Bengali saree (deep red and black cloth with old heavy gold ornaments), bare feet that make no sound, a faint silver mist around her; her presence always brings a strong musky fragrance

characters.name: Sadhu
characters.look: a very tall, very dark-skinned old sadhu with long matted grey hair tied on top, a long grey beard, bloodshot calm eyes, ash on his body, a red loincloth and a rudraksha mala, sitting on a seat of five skulls under a huge chhatim tree beside a ruined temple in a sal forest

characters.name: Matu Pagli
characters.look: Matu Pagli, a wild-eyed cremation-ground madwoman of about fifty, thin and dark, tangled grey-black hair, a torn dirty red saree, iron and conch bangles, a cracked laugh, who knows far more than she says

characters.name: Santhal woman
characters.look: a poor Santhal village woman of about thirty, dark skin, hair in a bun with a red flower, a simple white-and-red saree worn Santhal style, silver anklets, desperate tearful eyes

tantrik.setting: ENGLISH: A damp, dark room in 1940s Kolkata with peeling mustard-yellow walls, lit by a single flickering hurricane lamp casting long shadows, old wooden shelves piled with manuscripts, a small wooden cot where Kishori sits listening intently to old Taranath.
